title: The Semester of Cedar Falls
premise: In Cedar Falls, population 912, Paloma Voss has survived high school by keeping her head down and her truths small. When her AP English teacher assigns a college essay prompt — 'Describe a moment you knew the truth would cost you' — every anonymous submission lands in a shared folder that gets leaked, including one essay revealing that beloved drama teacher Mr. Reyes covered up an assault by a star athlete years ago. As the town splits into camps, Paloma, who wrote about being outed against her will, must decide whether to defend Mr. Reyes, who once protected her, or the girl whose essay started it all. In the end, she testifies at the school board hearing, loses her best friend and nearly her scholarship audition, but gains a chosen family of truth-tellers — and learns that survival isn't silence.
about_author: L. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former debate coach who grew up in a town so small the school marquee doubled as the news station. They write stories about kids who learn that honesty is a group project.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Twelve
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet Cedar Falls through her wry, defensive narration: the only out kid, best friend Dani, safe harbor in Mr. Reyes's drama room. The college essay prompt is assigned. Emotional beat: guarded contentment that the reader already senses is fragile.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She drafts three fake essays before writing one honest paragraph about being outed by a leaked screenshot freshman year — then submits it half-hoping no one reads closely. Meanwhile, classmates grumble anonymously. Beat: the thrill and terror of saying one true thing.

chapters.title: Folder: Shared
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with quiet classmate Juniper Okafor, whose essay accuses Mr. Reyes of burying her sister's assault report to protect athlete Cole Brandt. The folder leaks schoolwide overnight. Beat: dread crystallizing into public catastrophe.

chapters.title: Sides
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The town picks teams: Dani defends Mr. Reyes fiercely; Juniper becomes a pariah; Cole's family threatens lawsuits. Paloma stays silent, protecting her audition slot and her friendship. Beat: complicity dressed up as prudence.

chapters.title: What He Did for Me
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Paloma's POV. Mr. Reyes shielded her after the screenshot incident, gave her the stage when nothing else felt safe. Now he asks her — quietly, not manipulatively — to remember that. Beat: loyalty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: Juniper's Table
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Paloma sits with Juniper at lunch, the first person to do so in weeks. Juniper shows her the police report her sister filed, the one that vanished. Beat: the slow, uncomfortable birth of belief.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Scholarship panel day collides with the school board hearing announcement. Dani discovers Paloma met with Juniper and calls it betrayal; their friendship fractures onstage mid-audition. Paloma falters but finishes. Beat: the first real price of choosing.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, unraveling. She rereads her own essay and hates how small she made her truth. She confronts Mr. Reyes, who admits what he buried and why — fear, debt, a family to protect. Beat: grief for a flawed protector; clarity arriving anyway.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the board hearing, Paloma reads her unedited essay aloud, then Juniper's sister's report, naming names. The room detonates; Cole withdraws from state finals under investigation; Mr. Reyes resigns, thanking her bitterly and honestly. Beat: truth as an act with casualties.

chapters.title: Ensemble Cast
chapters.summary: Resolution, Paloma's POV. Weeks later: Dani, changed, shows up at rehearsal with coffee and no apology yet — just presence. Juniper and Paloma found an anonymous zine publishing the essays that started everything. Paloma auditions again, singing her own words. Beat: found family, scarred but real; survival redefined as voice.
